description: The model ladder the router chooses from. Everything the router prompt and the resolver need is data here: add a model by appending to a level's models, add a level by inserting an object into levels, hide a level that has no rostered model with shown:false. The router chain's order, each router's max_input_tokens, its transport (cli, or direct_chat straight to the local server with temperature and seed), thinking_off (a reply that reports thinking tokens fails the attempt) and an optional confirm rule (ask the next router when this one picks above a level or picks the local level for an unqualified shape) are data in router.chain. lib/router_catalog.py validates this file strictly; lib/route_resolve.py applies it.

effort.ceiling_rule: Never request an effort above the ceiling. xhigh and max exist in the roster for some models and stay unused until the user approves a specific task.

meaning.low: Mechanical, lookup or clearly bounded work. Resolves to the model's lowest setting (Qwen3.6: off).
meaning.high: The level is right but the task has subtle logic, many cases, or a costly miss; more care on the same model is likely enough. Prefer this to moving up a level.

principles: Choose the lowest level and the lowest effort that will reliably do the work. Choosing too high is the common mistake. A choice that is too low is caught by review and by the escalation rule after two failed attempts.

Judge by what the work requires, not by how the request is worded. Length, urgency, the words careful, critical, security, credentials, production or safety, and a long list of constraints do not make a task harder. Risk is handled by the review field, not by the level.
A long request is usually long because it carries context and rules. Find the one thing the worker has to do and judge that.

Effort medium is the normal choice. Use high instead of moving up a level when the level is right but the task needs more care: subtle logic, many interacting cases, an adversarial review. Use low for mechanical, lookup or clearly bounded work. Nothing above high exists.
When torn between two adjacent levels, choose the lower one and, if care is the worry, raise the effort instead.

The top level is rare. Choose it only for a very large breadth of scope, typically an architecture across many subsystems, or for work that needs a great deal of inference to reach any answer. Applying a known pattern, however large, sensitive or security-related, is not that, and neither is a long or urgent request.
{level:local} requires a listed shape and a request that names its files or an exact command. If either is missing, use the next level up.

review.optional: Ordinary changes that are easy to check by running tests or reading a short diff.
review.required: Changes that touch permissions, secrets handling, deletion, data migration, concurrency, or anything hard to check by running a command, and every review of security-relevant code. The deterministic review policy still has the final word and can only raise this.

summarize_files.text: summarize or draft documentation from given files

levels.name: Local Qwen
levels.for: Bounded read-only or mechanical work whose files or exact command are named in the request and whose answer can be checked by reading the output: find and quote, count, short classification. Free and private.
levels.not_for: Anything that changes more than one file, designs, judges trade-offs, reviews security or concurrency, or whose result cannot be checked cheaply. Never the only reviewer. Not for large packets (the 32k Slotstream model cannot hold one).

anchors.task: Find where the request timeout default is set in config/net.py and quote the line.
How many test files under tests/ import load_profile? Give the number and the file names.

levels.name: Haiku / GPT-6 luna
levels.for: Small, well-specified jobs with an obvious approach and an easy check: one named-file edit plus its check command, run named tests and report, look something up across a few files, summarize or draft short text from given material, a mechanical change. Also what a {level:local} job becomes when it lacks a listed shape.
levels.not_for: Choosing between designs, subtle bugs, reviewing a non-trivial diff, anything where a wrong answer would look plausible.

anchors.task: Change the default page size in settings.py from 20 to 50 and run tests/test_settings.py.
Run the unit tests for the parser module and report which fail with the first error line of each.
Summarize the three attached design notes into ten bullet points.

levels.name: Sonnet / GPT-6 sol
levels.for: The ordinary software work and the default: a feature, a bug fix, tests, a focused investigation, a review of a normal diff, a routine design with an obvious best option. Effort medium by default; high for subtle correctness, adversarial or security-relevant review, or work across several components.
levels.not_for: An architecture across many subsystems or work that needs a great deal of inference. Trivial lookups and one-line edits.

anchors.task: Add pagination to the /orders endpoint with tests, following the existing list endpoints.
The nightly export drops rows when a customer has two billing addresses. Find the cause and fix it.
Review this 200-line diff to the cache invalidation code for correctness bugs.
Review a change to the payment retry logic for double-charge and ordering bugs.
Three modules each implement their own retry policy. Propose how to unify them and weigh two obvious designs.

levels.name: GPT sol 6.1
levels.for: Hard work with a known approach where Sonnet at high effort is likely to miss things: a very large review or refactor, an audit across many components, a long careful investigation. Rare. No Claude model sits at this level today.
levels.not_for: Anything Sonnet at high effort can reasonably do. Architecture across many subsystems or deep inference (that is the top level).

anchors.task: After a change to the shared invoice library's rounding rules, check every consumer across eleven services for rounding and currency bugs and list each with a fix.
Review a 1,500-line change that moves the scheduler's locking across five modules, checking every lock order.

models.unverified: listed by pi, not in config/router.json yet; efforts assumed to match gpt-6-sol

levels.name: Opus / GPT-6 astra
levels.for: Work with a very large breadth of scope, typically an architecture or design across many subsystems, or work that needs a great deal of inference to reach any answer. Expected to be rare: a small fraction of tasks. The level is also reached by an explicit request and by escalation after two failed attempts; you cannot see those, and they are never a reason for you to choose it.
levels.not_for: Anything a mid-level model at high effort can do, however long, urgent, risky or security-related. Reviews of ordinary or even large diffs. Applying a known pattern. Security wording, length and risk never raise the level.

anchors.task: Design the target architecture for splitting a monolith into services: eleven subsystems share state, and the order of the migration and every interface between them must be decided.
Reconcile the data model, sync protocol, auth and billing designs of a product spanning nine subsystems into one coherent architecture, deriving the constraints each imposes on the others.
